profile.name: Tello
profile.tagline: A rhythmic Azerbaijani folk dance performed in a line with linked fingers.
profile.insight: Dancers hold each other by the little fingers with arms raised to shoulder level, moving their shoulders in rhythm during two distinct fast-paced sections.
profile.profile: Tello is an Azerbaijani national dance categorized as a type of yalli. It is performed by both men and women across various regions of Azerbaijan. The dance is characterized by a specific hand-linking technique and rhythmic shoulder movements.
profile.profile_long:
Tello is a traditional Azerbaijani dance that belongs to the yalli family of folk dances. It is a social dance performed by both men and women, reflecting a shared cultural practice found across almost all regions of Azerbaijan. The name of the dance is associated with a female name, though specific historical details regarding its origin are not described in sources. 

The performance of Tello is defined by its specific physical formation and upper-body engagement. Dancers link together by holding the little fingers of their neighbors, maintaining this connection with their arms raised to shoulder level. The dance is structured into two distinct fast-paced sections. Throughout these sections, the dancers perform rhythmic movements, specifically moving their shoulders up and down in coordination with the tempo. As a type of yalli, it is a collective dance that emphasizes synchronization among participants. Because the sources do not provide information on specific footwork, musical accompaniment, or traditional attire, the dance is primarily documented through its characteristic hand-linking and shoulder-focused movement pattern.
